decision_boundary: This saved-result review supports a startup-focused release with preserved default output and complete disclosure of comparison losses. It does not approve publication itself, prove faster recall, pass the original 10/15/10 recall gates, or establish superiority in every dimension. Final exact-commit CI, packaging, release and published-install gates remain the release owner responsibility.
findings: Complete non-timing default payloads match v0.3.3 for all 1536 native pairs and 768 component pairs; all 42 quality cells and 6912 calls are complete.

Candidate native mean latency is higher in all six cells. Five of six native p50 and p95 cells are higher; o200k_base/512 is lower. These are sequential descriptive observations, not the preregistered ABBA recall gate.

Candidate component mean, p50 and p95 are higher than v0.3.3 across pooled native search, adapter, first-pass, repeat and first-pass-plus-all-reads surfaces. Setup and existing-book-open times are also slightly higher in this run.

Against the pinned claude-mem retrieval component, candidate evidence recall, complete evidence and MRR are higher at all six axes, while individual question and annotation losses still occur and are retained.

Against ai-memory, candidate evidence recall and complete evidence rates are lower at every axis. Against billion-context, evidence recall is lower at every axis and complete evidence is lower at 1024/2048. Candidate MRR is higher than each pinned component across these aggregate cells; that does not negate the evidence losses.

billion-context is faster in the recorded component search surfaces and keeps no persistent corpus state. Book raw search payload token counts are higher than all three external components. Component scope, response content and native read policies differ.

Candidate native sampled RSS exceeds baseline. Candidate component sampled RSS is lower, but sampler wall time is higher. The sampled worker includes the evaluator and corpus, and finalization peaks include harness work.

Candidate component raw search payload mean is 0.0078125 tokens higher under each tokenizer. Timing-inclusive raw JSON differs in latency_ms; all complete non-timing payload hashes match, so this is not evidence-content growth.

ai-memory has zero unmapped native hits in this cohort and all 1280 requested page reads are counted. Its after-close zero bytes reflect temporary state deletion, not a durable zero-footprint product.
limitations: This fixed public cohort has 256 answerable questions, 619 evidence annotations and zero overlap with the 896 prior selected questions; it does not measure no-answer behavior, generated-answer accuracy, or every real workload.
Only the pinned retrieval components and exact source/runtime identities were exercised. No whole-product superiority or arbitrary production-scale extrapolation is supported.
Native Book recall and supplied-page component evaluation use different assembly boundaries; native and component latency numbers must not be mixed into one ratio.
Fresh latency is sequential, with first/repeat subsets disclosed, not randomized ABBA confirmation. No timing threshold was relaxed and no run or sample was replaced.
Offline packing latency is evaluator cost. It is separately retained and must not be described as native search latency.

Resource peaks are 20 ms observations of worker and live descendants, include evaluator/corpus and may double-count shared mappings. They are lower bounds on observed process RSS, not unique physical product memory.
Storage counts regular-file content lengths, excluding symlinked caches, not filesystem allocation. Lifecycle and persistence differ across components.
Output equality and clear startup gains support the disclosed release scope; they do not turn the preserved retrieval slowdowns or competitor quality losses into gains.
